chunks: And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from Hishām ibn Sālim, from al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام, who said:

The world is both a seeker and one being sought. Whoever seeks the world, death will pursue him until it removes him from it. And whoever seeks the Hereafter, the world will pursue him until it delivers his sustenance to him.

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: the worldly life and its immediate concerns
key_terms.الْآخِرَةَ: the Hereafter, the final abode after worldly life
key_terms.الْمَوْتُ: death, which inevitably overtakes every person

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام teach about seeking the dunya versus seeking the Hereafter?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that attachment to the dunya does not secure it, because death inevitably overtakes the one who chases it. But the one whose aim is the Hereafter will still receive the rizq decreed for him in the world. It calls the believer to reorder priorities around the akhirah rather than worldly pursuit.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5886 - Ali ibn Al-Hakam narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), who said:
"The world is both a seeker and one being sought.
Whoever seeks the world, death will pursue him until it removes him from it.
And whoever seeks Hereafter, the world will pursue him until it delivers his sustenance to him."
